_about: Reviewed VEX default per KB finding code (CB-22, rules cb22-1) and whether each CVE a finding code maps to is a flaw of the algorithm or protocol itself. Hand-written and reviewed: one row per code with its basis (observed -> exploitable; posture, quantum_only, inferred, static -> in_triage), the reason and its sources; one row per mapped CVE with inherent true/false. build_kb.py copies basis and reason into each KB entry as vex_default, and inherent into each CVE record as vex_inherent; it fails on a missing or extra row, an unknown basis, a quantum-only KB entry not marked quantum_only, or an observed basis in the code namespace.

CVE-2004-2761.reason: MD5 is not collision resistant: a flaw of the algorithm

CVE-2005-4900.reason: SHA-1 is not collision resistant: a flaw of the algorithm

CVE-2009-3555.reason: TLS renegotiation flaw fixed by the RFC 5746 extension in implementations

CVE-2011-3389.reason: BEAST: needs a client without the 1/n-1 split; mitigated client-side in current browsers

CVE-2012-4929.reason: CRIME: needs TLS compression enabled, not observed by the matching code

CVE-2013-0169.reason: Lucky Thirteen: an implementation timing side channel, fixed in libraries

CVE-2013-2566.reason: RC4 single-byte biases: a flaw of the cipher

CVE-2014-0224.reason: CCS injection: an OpenSSL implementation bug

CVE-2014-3566.reason: POODLE: a flaw of the SSL 3.0 protocol's CBC padding

CVE-2015-0204.reason: FREAK: an OpenSSL client implementation bug (plus export suites)

CVE-2015-2808.reason: RC4 key-scheduling weakness (Bar Mitzvah): a flaw of the cipher

CVE-2015-4000.reason: Logjam: a flaw of the TLS protocol with DHE_EXPORT and small DH groups

CVE-2016-0800.reason: DROWN: a flaw of the SSLv2 protocol (cross-protocol attack on the shared RSA key)

CVE-2016-2183.reason: SWEET32: the birthday bound of 64-bit block ciphers
